definition: Belated means coming later than it should have.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word belated. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know belated should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Marco's belated birthday card reached his sister in March, complete with an apology and a drawing of a very slow snail.
Tardy is the mildest rung — a tardy student misses five minutes of class; belated arrivals are measured in seasons and years.
Overdue stops short of belated: an overdue book is past its date but still expected back, while a belated tribute turns up after everyone has stopped waiting.

Delayed means held up: an obstacle — weather, a backlog, a slow train — got in the way, and the thing is still coming. A belated gesture met no obstacle at all; it simply arrived after the moment it was owed had passed. Delayed blames the route; belated admits the lateness.

Unpunctual describes a person and a habit — someone routinely not on time, with no single occasion in view. Belated attaches to the gesture itself: the card, the tribute, the apology that arrives after its moment has passed. An unpunctual friend sends many belated birthday wishes.

Belated means coming later than it should have, and the should is the sting.
A slow train is merely delayed; a belated repair, apology, or thank-you arrives after the moment it was owed has mostly passed.
The thing still counts — winter, however, is over.
Belated is the word for gestures that arrive after their moment — apologies, congratulations, recognitions, repairs.

It carries a small bow of acknowledged fault, which is why greeting cards say "happy belated birthday" and not "happy tardy birthday." Keep tardy for everyday small lateness and overdue for deadlines still in force; belated is for the moment already gone.

Three years later the old span failed exactly as she had predicted.
